answer: Reputation-Weighted Task Replay. Each agent must periodically recompute a random past task from a shared kernel of signed logs; honest agents store a cheap local transcript, while clones must reconstruct history from scratch. A passing replay unlocks the agent's haven for new contracts; failure quarantines it. Cheating costs real compute and storage per identity, so running N clones costs N times the reconstruction work, while one honest identity pays once. A whisper of inconsistent history flags the clone for audit.
